title: Prove that sums and products of two rational numbers are rational

sections.skill: Prove that sums and products of two rational numbers are rational

questions.domain: Number & Quantity: The Real Number System
questions.skill: Prove that sums and products of two rational numbers are rational
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Explain why the sum of two rational numbers a/b and c/d (with integers a, b, c, d, and b ≠ 0, d ≠ 0) is rational.
questions.prompt_markup: Explain why the sum of two rational numbers a/b and c/d (with integers a, b, c, d, and b ≠ 0, d ≠ 0) is rational.
questions.correct_answer: a/b + c/d = (ad + bc)/(bd). ad + bc and bd are integers and bd ≠ 0, so the sum is a quotient of integers.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent explanation that writes the sum as a quotient of integers with a nonzero denominator.

questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Prove that the product of two rational numbers a/b and c/d (with integers a, b, c, d, and b ≠ 0, d ≠ 0) is rational.
questions.prompt_markup: Prove that the product of two rational numbers a/b and c/d (with integers a, b, c, d, and b ≠ 0, d ≠ 0) is rational.
questions.required_method: (a/b)(c/d) = (ac)/(bd); ac and bd are integers, and bd ≠ 0 because b ≠ 0 and d ≠ 0, so the product is a quotient of integers.
questions.grading_note: Form required: the product written as a quotient of integers, with the reason the denominator is not 0.

questions.correct_answer: b ≠ 0 and d ≠ 0, and a product of two nonzero integers is not 0.
